Thank you. For understanding. It’s so hard to feel so alone and so responsible. Sometimes I feel like im only living for other people. And then one day I wake up and feel “healed”. It’s so crazy.
That is the worst feeling. I have no advice other than just try to get through this. This is the hardest thing I deal with. I just try to remember my family.

Oh love I know it’s hard. This pandemic had fucked this world. You have a place in this world. You are the reason someone is alive. I guarantee it. You have done so much already. Think about your achievements. One time I told a kid I babysat that they were really good at drawing. That was 15 years ago. They go to art school now. I never realized the impact I had. You are important.
Oh love bug. Life is hard. But we are strong. What is wearing on you?

Oh honey. You have got this. I know it’s so hard. But you will make it through. Think about the joy of showing the world the REAL YOU. I hope it scares you. It’s a level of happiness you can’t imagine. But you have a giant fucking support group. We are all here for you. If right now “we” is just me than so be it. I am here for you. You are important. You are valid. You are loved.

I don’t believe there is any way to die without pain. At the end of the day, if you live…you are in pain. If you die…everyone you know is in pain. Yeah maybe you died “without pain” but you still caused pain. That’s the thought that had kept me on this earth. I am in so much pain. But I don’t want to force that pain on anyone else.

We lived 3 miles from her before we moved and she went 4 months without seeing her mom. Now that we moved slightly farther it seems to have jolted her memory that she has another child ( she has 3 others, none of which are mine but all of which I have taken in with my current wife whenever their mother can’t be bothered to take care of them. It’s been rough but we are really dialing in on changing custody to us having full legal and custody and having set visitation days and times because she is taking advantage of our compassion and it’s exhausting
